plan.name: Render checked reader charts as standalone SVG
plan.summary: Add (*statechart.Result).SVG() (string, error), a shared standalone renderer that computes its layout and writes SVG in Go for the complete checked ordinary chart, including every initial state, directed labeled arrow, self-loop, parallel and reverse arrow, and multiline or long reader label. Preserve the full Result in inert JSON metadata and display its bounded-model qualifications, rule wording, violations, unavailable actions, hidden steps, counts, provenance and advisory arrow target; retain the existing Mermaid publication behavior and check topology agreement with acceptance tests, without adding receipt or dashboard integration. The output is deterministic, accessible, self-contained literal XML with generated element IDs, no active content or external resources, a viewBox containing the drawing and report, and sufficient spacing and label sizing to keep loops, parallel arrows and labels distinct; rendering never mutates the input or silently drops data, and malformed chart structure or text XML cannot represent returns an error and no SVG. Offline acceptance tests inspect actual SVG topology, geometry, text, metadata and resource references, exercise the 500-state capacity without an arrow cutoff, and check repeated and concurrent rendering against the existing computation and Mermaid tests, whose pinned behavior remains unchanged. Update SPEC.md with existing supporting decision citations D-0335, D-0343, D-0105, D-0122 and D-0294, the README's short linked description within its 400-line budget, and docs/statecharts.md with the delivered API and SVG contract; the merger records the new native-rendering decision because this plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestSVG608TopologyAndGeometry
tests.says: Every checked state, initial and visible arrow is drawn, with separate directed paths for loops, parallel and reverse arrows, readable node boxes, and a finite positive viewBox.

tests.name: TestSVG608LiteralLabelsAndAccessibility
tests.says: Long, multiline, Unicode and markup-like labels remain literal and complete, have room to be read, and cannot introduce active XML or external resources; the SVG has a meaningful accessible title and description.

tests.name: TestSVG608ReportAndMetadata
tests.says: The SVG preserves the entire checked result and displays bounds, exact rules, state qualifications, hidden occurrences, independent counts and their meanings, provenance and temporal facts without adding a proof claim.

tests.name: TestSVG608SupportedCapacity
tests.says: A computed chart at the existing 500-state capacity renders every state and all 999 arrows, including its advisory over-target qualification, without sampling or an additional arrow cutoff.

tests.name: TestSVG608DeterministicAndReadOnly
tests.says: Repeated and concurrent renders of the same checked input are byte-identical, do not mutate any input, and work with no rendering executables on PATH.

tests.name: TestSVG608RejectsUnrenderableInput
tests.says: Nil, empty, unsupported or structurally inconsistent charts and XML-inexpressible text fail explicitly with no partial SVG.

tests.name: TestSVG608MatchesPublishedMermaid
tests.says: The native SVG and the existing factory Mermaid serializer represent identical checked states, initials and labeled directed arrows, including loops, parallel edges and literal special characters.
